author: reek
body: The boot-time replay walks the fact log and rebuilds the in-memory store. It has to survive two things this test puts in front of it.

author: reek
body: A fact is not one sector. pack-fact-entry has always sized itself with sectors-for-fact, and app-write-fact -- the writer the repository protocol uses -- writes as many sectors as the content needs. A source definition is thousands of bytes. The replay used to read a single sector, refuse anything longer, and return the store it had built so far, which ended the walk. One multi-sector fact truncated the whole store at that entry: every fact behind it sat on the disk, intact and verifiable, and was invisible. The superblock kept reporting the full count, so nothing looked wrong.

author: reek
body: A corrupt fact ended the walk for the same reason. The honest response to one bad entry is to skip that entry, not to discard every entry behind it.
